solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Andhra Pradesh's official language is **Telugu**. It is one of the classical languages of India and has a rich literary tradition.
 
• Kerala's official language is **Malayalam**. Malayalam is spoken by the majority of the people in Kerala and has a significant cultural and historical background.
 
• Karnataka's official language is **Kannada**. Kannada is another classical language of India and has a profound literary heritage.
 
• Goa's official languages include **Konkani**. Konkani is widely spoken in Goa and is also one of the 22 scheduled languages of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andhra Pradesh**

 
 
• Andhra Pradesh is a state in the southeastern coastal region of India.
 
• It was bifurcated to form the new state of Telangana in 2014.
 
• It is known for its rich cultural heritage and historical significance.
 
 
 
• **Kerala**
 
 
• Kerala is a state on the southwestern Malabar Coast of India.
 
• It is known for its backwaters, beaches, and rich tradition of classical arts and dance forms like Kathakali.
 
• Kerala has the highest literacy rate among Indian states.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**
 
 
• Karnataka is a state in the southwestern region of India.
 
• It is known for its technology hub, Bengaluru, and historical sites like Hampi and Mysore.
 
• Karnataka is also a prominent center of classical Indian music and dance.
 
 
 
• **Goa**
 
 
• Goa is a state on the southwestern coast of India within the region known as the Konkan.
 
• It was a Portuguese colony until 1961.
 
• Goa is renowned for its beaches, Portuguese heritage, and vibrant tourism industry.
